examples.text: Может, пойдёшь сегодня вечером с нами?
examples.trans: Maybe you will come out with us tonight?

examples.text: Отлично, тогда до встречи вечером!
examples.trans: Great, then see you in the evening!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'hour' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Смотри, твой су-шеф сейчас звонит.
examples.trans: Look, your sous-chef is calling right now.

examples.text: Лёва, какую ерунду ты сейчас говоришь?
examples.trans: Lyova, what nonsense are you talking right now?

examples.text: Завтра в два часа в поликлинике?
examples.trans: Tomorrow at two o'clock at the clinic?

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Кате точно нужно надёжное мужское плечо.
examples.trans: Katya definitely needs a reliable man's shoulder.

examples.text: Прости, мне нужно нести заказ.
examples.trans: Forgive me, I need to carry the order.

examples.text: Мне через час нужно срочно отъехать.
examples.trans: I need to leave urgently in an hour.

meanings.en: urgently, right away; predicative: it is urgent
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Мне через час нужно срочно отъехать.
examples.trans: I need to leave urgently in an hour.

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, это срочно!
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent!

examples.text: Мне нужно срочно позвонить.
examples.trans: I need to make a phone call urgently.

отъехать.gloss: to step away / drive off briefly

meanings.en: to step away / drive off briefly
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'ъехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to step away / drive off briefly'.

related.gloss: not to to step away (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Мне через час нужно срочно отъехать.
examples.trans: I need to leave urgently in an hour.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и отъехать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to step away on time.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'go, walk', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.text: Прости, пожалуйста, мне пора идти работать.
examples.trans: Excuse me, please, it is time for me to go work.

examples.text: Я иду домой.
examples.trans: I'm going home.

examples.text: Он идёт на второй срок.
examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

meanings.en: to meet, to greet, to pick up
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'тречать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to meet, to welcome', paired with 'встретить'.

examples.text: Иди встречай Аню, они уже пришли!
examples.trans: Go greet Anya, they have already arrived!

examples.text: Ладно, хорошо, уже бегу встречать!
examples.trans: Alright, fine, I am already running to greet them!

examples.text: Вас и не должны были встречать.
examples.trans: Nobody was supposed to meet you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты уже закончил работу, Лёва?
examples.trans: Have you finished work already, Lyova?

examples.text: Неужели в анализах что-то не так?
examples.trans: Could something really be wrong in the tests?

examples.text: Всё хорошо, мы уже скоро поедем.
examples.trans: Everything is fine, we will be going soon.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'came', paired with 'приходить'.

examples.text: Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Security will be here any moment.

examples.text: Я приду завтра.
examples.trans: I'll come tomorrow.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Ладно, давай закажем себе по коктейлю.
examples.trans: Alright, let us order ourselves a cocktail each.

examples.text: Ладно, я тогда пойду, не буду мешать.
examples.trans: Alright, I will go then, I will not bother you.

examples.text: Да ладно, Костя, я совсем не против.
examples.trans: Come on, Kostya, I do not mind at all.

meanings.en: to run (in one direction), to flee, to escape
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'am running', paired with 'побежать'.

examples.text: Беги, Марина, пока не поздно!
examples.trans: Run, Marina, before it's too late!

examples.text: Куда ты так быстро бежишь?
examples.trans: Where are you running so fast?

examples.text: Надо бежать! Беги в деревню к маме.
examples.trans: You need to run! Run to the village to your mum's.
